title: Building for agents
slideTitles: My tools have two users: me and a coding agent.
I ship a change with seven tools I built.
Stacks briefs the agent and checks its work.
The Stacks CLI is written with Effect.
Stacks output differs for people and agents.
foreman runs each Codex task in its own worktree.
foreman is a short-lived CLI and a daemon.
Codex waits until Claude answers its question.
rr runs each agent's tests on its own machine.
StatGlass started as the rr monitor command.
Rust collects the data and TypeScript draws it.
The StatGlass UI also runs in a browser tab.
Agents read StatGlass history through a CLI.
OpenData sends text to the model, rows to the UI.
OpenChart validation reports which field is wrong.
A Decks hook blocks AI-sounding sentences.
Each tool has some of the same six habits.
The seven tools are at steamfield.io.

states.lead: rr --pretty prints a summary for a person.
states.body: One line per task with its host and time, then totals. Designing this view is developer experience, DX.

states.lead: A coding agent receives every byte.
states.body: The colour codes are part of the text, and each one uses space in the agent’s context.

states.lead: Without the flag, rr prints JSON events.
states.body: The last event lists each failing test. Designing this output is agent experience, AX.

states.lead: I built each tool for my own work.
states.body: Most started inside OpenData, whose test suite is about 14,000 tests.

states.lead: Six of the seven use TypeScript.
states.body: rr is Go. StatGlass samples the system in Rust, and OpenData’s engine is Python.

states.lead: Three get several slides tonight.
states.body: Stacks, foreman and StatGlass, with the source code on screen.

states.lead: One command writes the brief.
states.body: It writes starter files, agent instructions and a 4,481-word BRIEF.md.

states.lead: The agent’s prompt is two sentences.
states.body: It names the brief and says the work is done when stacks verify passes.

states.lead: The first verify run failed.
states.body: Claude Code ran it 393 seconds in and 5 of 15 steps failed. The next run passed at 501 seconds.

states.lead: Stacks refuses to verify edited checks.
states.body: Stacks keeps a hash of the steps outside the project and refuses to run if one was edited.

states.lead: Every run starts in three files.
states.body: bin.ts imports from Node, main.ts maps errors to exit codes, and cli.ts builds the command tree.

states.lead: Each command is one file.
states.body: It declares its flags, calls the core, and lists its exit codes in the help text.

states.lead: A service class includes its test double.
states.body: Host.layer wraps the real process and Host.memory is the fake the tests use.

states.lead: One function composes the layers.
states.body: It adds config, output, logging and processes, and the tests call the same function.

states.lead: Each error has one row in a table.
states.body: The row sets its exit code and whether a retry can work. A missing row fails the build.

states.lead: Tests replace a layer with a fake.
states.body: This test swaps in an HTTP client that returns 503, then checks the JSON error.

states.lead: On a terminal, verify prints colour.
states.body: Stacks uses this format only when stdout is a terminal, no agent is detected and CI is unset.

states.lead: Run by an agent, verify prints plain text.
states.body: Stacks finds an agent marker in the environment and prints no colour codes and no live step output.

states.lead: With --json, stdout is one object.
states.body: The last line of stderr is an error envelope whose next field says what to do.

states.lead: Each exit code has one meaning.
states.body: 5 means read the verify report, and 6 means ask a person.

states.lead: Claude writes one contract per task.
states.body: Each contract is a Markdown file. foreman reads its May change line for the paths the delegate may edit.

states.lead: foreman creates a worktree and branch per delegate.
states.body: The worktree is .claude/worktrees/<name> and the branch is foreman/<name>.

states.lead: site-commands asked Claude a question.
states.body: The daemon leaves the tool call open until Claude answers, and the other two delegates keep running.

states.lead: Claude answered after 18 seconds.
states.body: The answer is returned inside the same Codex turn, so the delegate continues with its context.

states.lead: Claude reviews each diff and commits it.
states.body: foreman leaves the work uncommitted. Its digest lists every file changed outside May change.

states.lead: The CLI exits and the daemon keeps running.
states.body: The daemon supervises every run and exits after 30 idle minutes.

states.lead: The CLI and daemon use a Unix socket.
states.body: Each message is one line of JSON. The CLI starts the daemon when the socket is missing.

states.lead: One codex app-server process runs every delegate.
states.body: The daemon sends it JSON-RPC over stdio and routes replies by thread id.

states.lead: foreman checks the Codex protocol by hash.
states.body: The hash covers 467 schema files from Codex 0.166.0. foreman doctor prints whether it still matches.

states.lead: Codex asks by calling the ask_orchestrator tool.
states.body: The daemon stores the request id and sends no response, so the Codex turn stays blocked.

states.lead: A background foreman wait exits with the question.
states.body: Claude Code reports the finished background task to Claude, which reads the question from its output.

states.lead: Claude's answer is returned as the tool result.
states.body: After 15 minutes without an answer, the daemon returns a message telling Codex to continue.

states.lead: The timeout test advances a test clock.
states.body: Effect's TestClock moves time by one second. A 117-line script replaces Codex in the tests.

states.lead: Each rr call is a separate process.
states.body: The only state they share is a lock on each host. rr has no server.

states.lead: A parallel task locks every host.
states.body: Its shards are tasks the config lists under parallel. rsync copies the files and SSH runs the command.

states.lead: A run waits when every host is locked.
states.body: It retries every 2 seconds and prints a waiting event with the command that holds the lock.

states.lead: A retry locks the first free host.
states.body: Each git worktree syncs to its own remote directory unless the config turns that off.

states.lead: The result event gives file and line.
states.body: rr parses pytest, Go test, Jest and Vitest output and reports each failed test's file, line and message.

states.lead: rr monitor shows each host in a terminal.
states.body: Each card has CPU, memory, latency and the command holding the host's lock, read over SSH.

states.lead: rr monitor keeps 600 samples per metric.
states.body: That is 10 minutes at one sample a second, held in memory until rr monitor exits.

states.lead: StatGlass keeps up to 30 days.
states.body: It is a menu bar app for Apple Silicon Macs that stores each host's history in SQLite.

states.lead: StatGlass is 58 percent Rust by lines.
states.body: Rust has the samplers, the SQLite store, remote hosts and the menu bar item. The React UI is TypeScript.

states.lead: tauri-specta generates bindings.ts.
states.body: It writes 92 commands and 10 events from the Rust source. A pre-push hook fails if the file is stale.

states.lead: Rust sends samples over a Tauri Channel.
states.body: Each tick is one message whose values are an array, ordered by a layout sent earlier.

states.lead: Each tick runs one transform animation.
states.body: d3 computes the path and React renders it as SVG. The animation slides the redrawn chart one slot.

states.lead: Idle CPU was 0.67 percent of one core.
states.body: Rust draws the menu bar item. Measured once, menu bar only, on an M3 Max in October 2026.

states.lead: React code calls a Transport interface.
states.body: One implementation calls Tauri and the other is a mock. A lint rule bans Tauri imports under src/app.

states.lead: The mock runs the app without Tauri.
states.body: Vitest, Playwright, the browser dev server and the docs site demo all use it.

states.lead: The statglass CLI reads recorded history.
states.body: now, history, events and top work on this Mac or on any remote host StatGlass mirrors.

states.lead: History output lists gaps in the samples.
states.body: The gap line gives the time range and the cause. Errors come back as JSON with a next step.

states.lead: The CLI is written in Rust.
states.body: The RFC estimates a compiled TypeScript binary at 55 to 60 MB, for a 36 MB app.

states.lead: The MCP server is TypeScript.
states.body: It registers 14 tools and runs on Bun with Hono. The query engine is Python and DuckDB.

states.lead: The server’s instructions set the tool order.
states.body: The order is search, then SQL, then chart. Search results already include column schemas.

states.lead: Chart rows go to the interface only.
states.body: The model reads the text. Up to 120 rows are in _meta, which the host shows only to the interface.

states.lead: The chart renders inside the chat.
states.body: The interface is a React app. The host loads it in an iframe from the server's ui:// resource.

states.lead: A chart is a JSON spec.
states.body: The spec names a mark and maps data columns to x and y. The engine computes the layout.

states.lead: The error names the misspelled field.
states.body: It has a JSON Pointer path, an error code, and a suggestion with the closest column name.

states.lead: With the field corrected, the spec validates.
states.body: validateSpec returns no errors and the Vue component draws the chart.

states.lead: Drawing is a separate package from the engine.
states.body: vanilla draws the engine's layout to the DOM. The React, Vue and Svelte packages wrap vanilla.

states.lead: Each click seeks the timeline to a beat.
states.body: The slide is a Vue component with a GSAP timeline. Stepping back plays the same tweens in reverse.

states.lead: The write hook enforces 5 lint patterns.
states.body: The lint has 27 patterns. A write matching one of the 5 errors is refused with the pattern's id.

states.lead: This deck lists a source for each figure.
states.body: Each row names the file or command that produces the figure.

states.lead: Six tools print JSON a program can parse.
states.body: The same six also print the next step, as a field or a line of text.

states.lead: A command checks when work is finished.
states.body: Stacks has verify, and Decks has check and lint. Three tools document one action per exit code.

states.lead: Agents run in parallel and read bundled docs.
states.body: rr locks a host and foreman uses a worktree per task. Five tools ship their own guide or skill.

states.lead: Any CLI or library can adopt these habits.
states.body: The six habits are output formats, exit codes, locks and bundled docs. None of them calls a model.
